samples.summary: No test asserts that one indent/outdent gesture is a single undo unit, though wrapping in `doc.batch()` is a headline behavior change of this diff
samples.evidence: Every editor entry point (`editor.ts` indent/outdent, `text-editor.ts` handleTab/handleIndent/handleOutdent, `text-box-editor.ts` indent/outdent) was rewritten to `doc.batch(() => { snapshot(); applyListLevelChanges(...); ... })`, with long comments claiming that without it "one Cmd+Z would leave the subtree half-moved". No test in the diff or in the tree calls `undo()` after an indent/outdent: `editor-tab-bullet.test.ts` only asserts post-edit `listLevel` arrays and painted x; the new text-box test only asserts the final committed blocks; the only undo assertions in docs tests are in `store/memory.test.ts`, `copy-integrity.test.ts`, `edit-link-in-place.test.ts`, `editor-page-setup.test.ts`, none of which touch list levels. So removing the `batch()` wrapper, or moving `snapshot()` back outside it, would not fail any test — the regression the change exists to prevent (half-moved subtree after one undo, and N Yorkie changes per gesture) can ship undetected.

samples.summary: Text-box editor list-level coverage is one happy-path case; boundaries and sibling isolation are untested there
samples.evidence: The single new text-box test builds `[a@0, b@1]`, runs `indent(); outdent(); indent();` and asserts only the final committed `[1, 2]`. It never asserts the intermediate outdent state, never covers the floor (outdent at level 0 must be a no-op for the subtree), the ceiling (MAX_LIST_LEVEL refusal), a following same-level sibling that must not be carried, or a multi-block selection through the text-box walker (whose signature changed to pass `doc.document.blocks`). Those paths are only covered at the pure-planner level in `test/model/list-level.test.ts`; the text-box wiring around them (`applyListLevelChanges`, the changed `forEachBlockInSelection`) is exercised by exactly one scenario.
searchedFor: read the new hunk in text-box-editor.test.ts

samples.summary: The switch from `layout.blockParentMap` to `doc.blockParentMap` (a caret inside a header/footer table cell) has no test
samples.evidence: `siblingsOf` and the cursor-only branch document at length that `layout.blockParentMap` resolves to `undefined` for a caret inside a header/footer table cell, which would silently make the gesture a no-op or walk the wrong container. The new tests cover a header list at top level (`list level in a header context`, `a header list carries its children too`) and a body table cell, but never a list inside a *header or footer table cell* — the exact case the map swap exists for. `grep header|footer` in editor-tab-bullet.test.ts finds only top-level header fixtures. A regression to `layout.blockParentMap` would keep every test green.
searchedFor: read the two new header describes

verdict.reason: The batch-grouping behavior is real in the source (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2701-2706 wraps saveSnapshot + applyListLevelChanges in doc.batch, mirrored in editor.ts and text-box-editor.ts), but no test anywhere asserts that an indent/outdent gesture is a single undo unit. editor-tab-bullet.test.ts (read in full, 672 lines) contains no undo/batch token and asserts only post-edit listLevel arrays, marginLeft and painted x. A repo-wide grep for `.undo(`/`undo()` yields 73 files; intersecting the docs test files that call undo with those that mention listLevel/indent leaves only test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts, whose undo coverage is a typeof/no-throw existence check (lines 351-359) and whose list test asserts only final committed levels (line 584). The nearest "one gesture = one undo step" assertions cover links (edit-link-in-place.test.ts:392,406) and the store seam in isolation (store/memory.test.ts:238), neither of which would fail if batch() were removed from the list-level paths. Frontend docs tests (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts listLevel hits are splitBlock/setBlockType; editor-undo-selection.test.ts has no list tokens) and model/list-level.test.ts (no undo/batch) also do not cover it; no e2e suite exists. Missing coverage over a change whose failure leaves a half-moved subtree after one Cmd+Z is user-visible/data-affecting, so major and blocking under the test-adequacy rubric.
